title.zh: 卷393 列傳一百八十 李星沅 周天爵 劳崇光
title.en: Volume 393 Biographies 180: Li Xingyuan, Zhou Tianjue, Lao Chongguang
title.raw: 卷393 列傳一百八十 李星沅 周天爵 劳崇光

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十李星沅，字石梧，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Biography 180: Li Xingyuan, styled Shiwo, a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 180 — Li Xingyuan, styled Shiwo, from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1832, entered the Hanlin as a probationary academician, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十五年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he supervised education in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was appointed provincial education commissioner for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 粵士多健訟，檄通省籍諸生之幹訟者，牒報诇治之，士風以肅。

translations.literal: Guangdong scholars were much given to litigation; he issued a proclamation throughout the province calling for reports on registered students who meddled in lawsuits, had them investigated and punished, and scholarly morale was thereby rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese literati were notoriously litigious. He circulated a province-wide edict requiring officials to report degree-holding students who acted as litigation brokers, had offenders investigated and disciplined, and thereby restored order among the scholarly class.

sentences.zh: 任滿，授陝西漢中知府，歷河南糧道，陝西、四川、江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was appointed prefect of Hanzhong in Shaanxi, and subsequently served as grain intendant of Henan and as surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was made prefect of Hanzhong in Shaanxi, then served successively as Henan grain intendant and as provincial judicial commissioner in Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 在川、陝嚴治刀匪、啯匪，屢擒其魁置之法。

translations.literal: In Sichuan and Shaanxi he strictly suppressed knife-bandits and geng-bandits, repeatedly capturing their ringleaders and executing them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan and Shaanxi he cracked down hard on armed bandit gangs, repeatedly capturing their leaders and putting them to death.

sentences.zh: 遷江西布政使，調江蘇。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Jiangxi, then reassigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jiangxi provincial treasurer and then transferred to the same post in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and concurrently served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was transferred to be governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲貴總督，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently acted as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou and concurrently served as acting governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 先是，永昌回亂，迤西道羅天池濫殺，不分良莠，眾回益擾。

translations.literal: Previously, during the Hui rebellion in Yongchang, Luo Tianchi, the circuit intendant of western Yunnan, had killed indiscriminately without distinguishing good from bad, and the Hui communities grew increasingly turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yongchang Muslim uprising, Luo Tianchi, the western Yunnan circuit intendant, had slaughtered indiscriminately without distinguishing loyal subjects from rebels, and Muslim unrest only worsened.

sentences.zh: 總督賀長齡、提督張必祿急於主撫，降者輒复叛。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Changling and Provincial Military Commander Zhang Bilu were eager to pursue pacification; those who surrendered promptly rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Changling and military commander Zhang Bilu were overeager to pacify by negotiation, and those who surrendered soon rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 至是，緬寧匪首馬國海被剿亡走，潛結雲州回馬登霄、海連升等復起事，迤西大震。

translations.literal: By this time the bandit chief Ma Guohai of Mianning, driven off by suppression campaigns, secretly joined with the Yunnan Hui leaders Ma Dengxiao, Hai Liansheng, and others to rise again, and western Yunnan was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebel leader Ma Guohai of Mianning, routed in suppression campaigns, had fled and secretly allied with the Yunzhou Muslims Ma Dengxiao and Hai Liansheng to revolt again, throwing all of western Yunnan into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 星沅追論肇亂之由，長齡、天池並獲譴。

translations.literal: Xingyuan traced back the causes of the original outbreak; both Changling and Tianchi were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan investigated the origins of the rebellion, and both He Changling and Luo Tianchi were censured.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遣兵進剿，解散被脅回眾，首逆就殲，餘匪肅清。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he dispatched troops to suppress them, disbanded the coerced Hui masses, the chief rebels were destroyed, and the remaining bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he sent troops on a punitive campaign, released Muslims who had been coerced into joining, destroyed the rebel leaders, and cleared out the remaining insurgents.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其功，加太子太保銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised his achievements, conferred upon him the honorary rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bestowed a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his service, granted him the honorary title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and awarded him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋調兩江總督。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to be governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 星沅未第時，客陶澍幕中，為掌章奏。

translations.literal: Before Xingyuan passed the examinations, he had been a guest in Tao Zhu's secretariat, where he was in charge of memorials and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Before earning his degree, Xingyuan had served on Tao Zhu's staff, drafting official memorials.

sentences.zh: 又歷官江南，習於鹽、漕、河諸利弊。

translations.literal: He had also held office in the Jiangnan region and was versed in the advantages and disadvantages of the salt monopoly, grain transport, and river conservancy systems.
translations.idiomatic: He had also served in the lower Yangtze region and was thoroughly familiar with the salt monopoly, grain transport, and river works.

sentences.zh: 時度支告匱，廷臣主南漕改徵折色解部，於北省採買。

translations.literal: At that time the treasury reported shortages, and court officials advocated converting southern tribute grain transport into cash payments to the Board of Revenue, with grain to be purchased in northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was strained, and court officials proposed converting southern tribute grain into cash payments to the Board of Revenue, with grain then purchased in the north.

sentences.zh: 星沅謂折多徵收不易，折少採買不敷。

translations.literal: Xingyuan said that if the conversion rate were set high, collection would be difficult, but if set low, purchases would fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan argued that a high conversion rate would make collection impractical, while a low rate would leave insufficient funds for purchase.

sentences.zh: 穀賤銀貴，民間展轉虧折。

translations.literal: Grain was cheap and silver dear, and the populace suffered repeated losses in conversion.
translations.idiomatic: With grain cheap and silver dear, ordinary people would lose money at every turn of the exchange.

sentences.zh: 且州縣藉端浮勒，胥吏高下其手，防之皆難。

translations.literal: Moreover, prefectures and counties would seize pretexts for extortionate levies, and clerks would manipulate rates at will — all of which would be hard to prevent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, local officials would seize any excuse to levy surcharges, and clerks would manipulate the rates at will — abuses nearly impossible to prevent.

sentences.zh: 迭疏論列，議遂寢。

translations.literal: He submitted repeated memorials setting forth these points, and the proposal was eventually shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial laying out these objections, and the proposal was eventually dropped.

sentences.zh: 淮鹽自陶澍整頓之後，歷年又多積欠。

translations.literal: Since Tao Zhu's reorganization of Huai salt, arrears had again accumulated year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tao Zhu's reforms of the Huai salt monopoly, arrears had again piled up year after year.

sentences.zh: 星沅疏陳引鹽壅積、課款支絀情形：「揆厥所由，官以畏難而因仍，商以畏難而取巧。

translations.literal: Xingyuan memorialized on the backlog of licensed salt and the shortfall in tax revenue: "Considering the root causes, officials, fearing difficulty, merely perpetuate old practices, while merchants, fearing difficulty, resort to expedients.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan memorialized on the glut of licensed salt and shortfalls in tax revenue: "At bottom, officials, afraid of hard work, simply perpetuate the status quo, while merchants, afraid of losses, resort to evasions.

sentences.zh: 成本增於雜費，行銷滯於售私，年復一年，幾同痼疾。

translations.literal: Costs rise through miscellaneous fees, and sales stagnate because of smuggling; year after year it has become nearly a chronic disease.
translations.idiomatic: Costs are inflated by surcharges, legitimate sales are undercut by smuggling, and year after year the system has grown nearly incurable.

sentences.zh: 先當以內清場私，外敵鄰私，為急則治標之計。

translations.literal: The urgent measure, treating the symptoms first, should be to clear internal field smuggling within our jurisdiction and resist neighboring smuggling from outside.
translations.idiomatic: The immediate priority — treating symptoms before the root cause — must be to suppress smuggling within our jurisdiction and block salt from neighboring regions.

sentences.zh: 本年回空糧私，奏請查禁。

translations.literal: This year, smuggling on returning empty grain boats — he memorialized requesting investigation and prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to investigate and ban smuggling aboard returning empty grain transport vessels.

sentences.zh: 其川私、墾私、潞私、浙私，均諮行堵緝。

translations.literal: As for Sichuan smuggling, reclaimed-land smuggling, Shanxi smuggling, and Zhejiang smuggling, he issued circulars to all concerned to block and seize.
translations.idiomatic: He issued circulars to block smuggling from Sichuan, reclaimed lands, Shanxi, and Zhejiang alike.

sentences.zh: 又引船夾帶，為害最鉅，扼要搜查，於揚州仙女廟及江寧下關緝獲百餘萬斤，提省審辦。

translations.literal: Smuggling by concealment on licensed transport boats was the greatest harm; he ordered searches at key points and at Yangzhou's Xiannü Temple and Jiangning's Xiaguan seized more than a million jin, which were sent to the province for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Concealed smuggling aboard licensed transport boats was the worst abuse; he ordered searches at strategic points and at Yangzhou's Fairy Temple and Nanjing's Xiaguan seized over a million jin of contraband salt, which was sent to the provincial capital for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 他如慎出納，提緩課，派懸引，刪繁文，配運殘引，提售新鹽，裁浮巡費，禁捏報淹銷，酌議章程八條，以圖整理。」

translations.literal: Other measures included careful accounting, advancing deferred tax payments, assigning outstanding licenses, cutting redundant paperwork, allocating transport of remnant licenses, advancing sale of new salt, reducing inflated patrol expenses, and prohibiting false reports of salt lost to flooding — eight articles of regulations were drafted to bring order."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed eight regulatory measures: strict accounting, advancing deferred payments, assigning outstanding licenses, cutting redundant paperwork, allocating transport of remnant licenses, advancing sales of new salt, reducing inflated patrol costs, and banning false reports of flood damage — all aimed at restoring order to the monopoly."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was referred to the relevant boards for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant boards for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 舊制，總督兼管河務，自道光二十二年後停止，至是復命兼管。

translations.literal: By old regulation the governor-general also supervised river works; this had ceased after the twenty-second year of Daoguang, but now he was again ordered to assume concurrent charge.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding custom the governor-general also oversaw river conservancy; this responsibility had been withdrawn after 1842, but now it was restored to him.

sentences.zh: 會兼署河督，疏請嚴禁廳員聚處清江，飭各歸工次。

translations.literal: When he concurrently acted as director-general of rivers, he memorialized requesting strict prohibition of bureau staff gathering at Qingjiang, ordering each to return to his work station.
translations.idiomatic: While concurrently serving as director-general of rivers, he memorialized to forbid bureau staff from congregating at Qingjiang and ordered each to return to his assigned work site.

sentences.zh: 奏籌外海水師事宜，曰磨厲人才，曰變通營巡，曰覈實會哨，曰扼要堵緝，曰配兵足數；

translations.literal: He memorialized on arrangements for the outer-sea naval forces, proposing to sharpen talent, reform patrol routines, verify joint patrols, block smuggling at key points, and ensure full complement of troops;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on coastal naval defense, proposing to develop talent, reform patrol routines, verify joint patrol meetings, block smuggling at strategic points, and ensure full troop complements;

sentences.zh: 又請添造戰船，勸捐給獎：並允行。

translations.literal: he also requested additional construction of warships and rewards for charitable donations: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: he also requested construction of additional warships and rewards for charitable donations — all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 俄羅斯通商舊由陸路，忽有商船至上海，執約拒之。

translations.literal: Russian trade had formerly been conducted by land routes; suddenly merchant vessels arrived at Shanghai, and he upheld the treaty provisions in refusing them.
translations.idiomatic: Russian trade had traditionally been conducted overland; when merchant vessels suddenly appeared at Shanghai, he upheld the treaty and turned them away.

sentences.zh: 在任兩年，宣宗甚加倚任。

translations.literal: During his two years in office, the Daoguang Emperor placed great trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: During his two years in office, the Daoguang Emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 因久病，請解職回籍，允之。

translations.literal: Because of chronic illness, he requested to resign and return home; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Plagued by chronic illness, he requested leave to resign and return home, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三十年，宣宗崩，赴京謁梓宮，復以母老陳請歸養。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Daoguang Emperor died; he went to the capital to pay respects at the coffin, and again petitioned to return home to care for his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850, when the Daoguang Emperor died, he went to the capital to pay respects at the coffin and again petitioned to return home to care for his elderly mother.

sentences.zh: 會廣西匪亂方熾，起林則徐督師，卒於途，命星沅代為欽差大臣。

translations.literal: Just then the bandit turmoil in Guangxi was raging; Lin Zexu had been recalled to command the campaign but died on the road, and Xingyuan was appointed Imperial Commissioner in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the rebellion in Guangxi was raging; Lin Zexu had been recalled to command the campaign but died en route, and Xingyuan was appointed Imperial Commissioner in his stead.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，抵廣西，駐柳州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, he reached Guangxi and established headquarters at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In December of that year he reached Guangxi and established headquarters at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時左右江匪氛蔓延，諸賊尤以桂平金田洪秀全為最悍。

translations.literal: At that time bandit activity spread along the Zuo and You Rivers, and among all the rebels Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guiping was the fiercest.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel activity had spread along the Zuo and You Rivers, and among all the insurgents Hong Xiuquan of Jintian in Guiping was the most formidable.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭祖琛、提督閔正鳳皆以貽誤黜去，週天爵、向榮繼為巡撫、提督。

translations.literal: Governor Zheng Zuchen and Military Commander Min Zhengfeng were both dismissed for dereliction; Zhou Tianjue and Xiang Rong succeeded them as governor and military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zheng Zuchen and military commander Min Zhengfeng were both dismissed for negligence; Zhou Tianjue and Xiang Rong succeeded them as governor and military commander respectively.

sentences.zh: 二人者並有重名，負意氣，議輒相左，星沅調和之，仍不協，軍事多牽掣。

translations.literal: Both men enjoyed great reputations and were proud in temperament; their counsel constantly clashed. Xingyuan tried to mediate, but they still could not cooperate, and military affairs were much hampered.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were famous and strong-willed; their counsel constantly clashed. Xingyuan tried to mediate, but they still could not cooperate, and military operations were repeatedly hamstrung.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，向榮進剿，賊由大黃江、牛排嶺竄新墟、紫荊山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xianfeng, Xiang Rong advanced to suppress them; the rebels fled from Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge to Xinxu and Zijing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1851, Xiang Rong advanced to suppress them; the rebels fled from the Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge toward Xinxu and Zijing Mountain.

sentences.zh: 星沅檄總兵秦定三、李能臣率滇、黔兵追躡，賊复竄武宣。

translations.literal: Xingyuan ordered Major-generals Qin Dingsan and Li Nengchen to lead Yunnan and Guizhou troops in pursuit; the rebels again fled to Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan ordered major-generals Qin Dingsan and Li Nengchen to pursue with Yunnan and Guizhou troops, but the rebels fled again to Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 榮、天爵各進擊，賊踞東鄉，兩軍攻之不克。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong and Zhou Tianjue each advanced to attack; the rebels held Dongxiang, and both armies failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong and Zhou Tianjue each advanced to attack, but the rebels held Dongxiang and both armies failed to dislodge them.

sentences.zh: 星沅以事權不一，奏請特簡總統將軍督剿，詔斥其推諉。

translations.literal: Xingyuan, citing divided command authority, memorialized requesting the special appointment of a supreme commanding general to direct suppression; an edict rebuked him for shirking responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Citing divided command, Xingyuan memorialized requesting the appointment of a supreme commander to direct the campaign; the throne rebuked him for shirking responsibility.

sentences.zh: 尋命大學士賽尚阿率總兵達洪阿、都統巴清德赴湖南防堵，將以代之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a was ordered to lead Major-general Da Hong'a and Banner Commander Ba Qingde to Hunan for defensive blocking, intending to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a was ordered to lead major-general Da Hong'a and banner commander Ba Qingde to Hunan on defensive duty, intending to replace him.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿至湖南，遂授欽差大臣，赴廣西督師，命星沅回湖南治防。

translations.literal: When Sai Shang'a reached Hunan, he was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangxi to command the army; Xingyuan was ordered back to Hunan to manage defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Sai Shang'a reached Hunan he was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangxi to take command; Xingyuan was ordered back to Hunan to manage defenses.

sentences.zh: 四月，星沅力疾赴武宣前敵督戰，至則已憊甚，數日卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Xingyuan, forcing himself despite illness, went to the front at Wuxuan to direct battle; upon arrival he was already greatly exhausted, and within several days died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In April, forcing himself despite illness, Xingyuan went to the front at Wuxuan to direct the fighting; he was already exhausted upon arrival and died in camp within days.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言：「賊不能平，不忠；

translations.literal: His deathbed memorial stated: "If the rebels are not pacified, I am disloyal;
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed memorial read: "If the rebels are not pacified, I have been disloyal;

sentences.zh: 養不能終，不孝。

translations.literal: if I cannot complete my filial duty of caring for my parent, I am unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: if I cannot fulfill my filial duty to my mother, I have been unfilial.

sentences.zh: 歿後斂以常服，用彰臣咎。」

translations.literal: After death, bury me in ordinary dress, to manifest this minister's guilt."
translations.idiomatic: After my death, bury me in ordinary dress, to make manifest this minister's guilt."

sentences.zh: 文宗覽而哀之，依總督例賜卹，賜金治喪，存問其母，子二人命俟服闋引見，諡文恭。

translations.literal: The Xianfeng Emperor read it with compassion, granted posthumous benefits according to the regulations for a governor, bestowed funds for the funeral, sent inquiries after his mother, ordered his two sons to be presented at court after their mourning period, and gave him the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng Emperor read it with compassion, granted posthumous benefits according to the regulations for a governor, bestowed funds for the funeral, sent inquiries after his mother, ordered his two sons to be presented at court after their mourning period, and gave him the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子桓，官至江西布政使。

translations.literal: His son Huan rose to the post of provincial treasurer of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan rose to serve as provincial treasurer of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 週天爵，字敬修，山東東阿人。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianjue, styled Jingxiu, a native of Dong'e in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tianjue, styled Jingxiu, from Dong'e in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，歸班銓選。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Jiaqing, he returned to await appointment through the regular selection process.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1811 and awaited appointment through the regular civil service selection process.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，授安徽懷遠知縣，調阜陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, he was appointed magistrate of Huaiyuan in Anhui, then transferred to Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was appointed magistrate of Huaiyuan in Anhui, then transferred to Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 天爵少以堅苦自立，篤信王守仁之學。

translations.literal: Tianjue from youth had established himself through steadfast hardship and was a devoted follower of Wang Shouren's philosophy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tianjue had built his career through steadfast self-discipline and was a devoted follower of Wang Yangming's philosophy.

sentences.zh: 及為令，盡心民事，廉介絕俗，皖北盜賊橫恣，與胥吏通，天爵極刑痛懲之。

translations.literal: When he became a magistrate, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to the people's affairs, was incorruptible beyond the common run, and when bandits ran rampant in northern Anhui in collusion with clerks, Tianjue punished them severely with extreme penalties.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he devoted himself wholeheartedly to public welfare, was incorruptible to a remarkable degree, and when bandits ran rampant in northern Anhui in collusion with local clerks, he punished them with the utmost severity.

sentences.zh: 有劾其殘酷者，總督蔣攸銛奏言：「天爵愛民如子，嫉惡如仇，古良​​吏也。」

translations.literal: Some impeached him for cruelty; Governor-General Jiang Youxian memorialized: "Tianjue loves the people as his children and hates evil as his enemy — he is an exemplary official of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Some impeached him for cruelty, but Governor-General Jiang Youxian memorialized: "Tianjue loves the people as his own children and hates evil as his own enemy — he is an official in the ancient mold."

sentences.zh: 由是受宣宗之知，諭曰：「不避嫌怨之員，最為難得，小過可宥之。」

translations.literal: Thereby he came to the Daoguang Emperor's notice; an edict stated: "An official who does not shrink from incurring resentment is most rare; minor faults may be forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he came to the Daoguang Emperor's notice; an edict declared: "An official who does not shrink from incurring resentment is most rare; minor faults may be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 連擢宿州知州、廬州知府、廬鳳潁泗道。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to prefect of Suzhou, prefect of Luzhou, and circuit intendant of Luzhou, Fengyang, Yingzhou, and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to prefect of Suzhou, prefect of Luzhou, and circuit intendant of the Luzhou-Fengyang-Yingzhou-Sizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 所至捕盜魁，無漏網者。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he captured bandit chiefs, with none escaping the net.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he captured bandit chiefs, leaving none at large.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢江西按察使，仍調安徽，遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi, still transferred to Anhui, then moved to provincial treasurer of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Jiangxi, transferred back to Anhui, and then promoted to provincial treasurer of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，署漕運總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he acted as director-general of grain transport, and shortly received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he served as acting director-general of grain transport and soon received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 時漕務積弊，運丁水手尤恣悍，特用天爵嚴馭之，劾衛官十二員以儆眾，詔褒勉之。

translations.literal: At that time the grain transport system had accumulated abuses, and transport coolies and boatmen were especially unruly; Tianjue was specially employed to discipline them strictly, impeached twelve transport-guard officials as a warning to all, and received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The grain transport system was riddled with abuses, and transport coolies and boatmen were especially unruly; Tianjue was specially appointed to discipline them, impeached twelve transport-guard officials as a warning to all, and received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調署湖廣總督，尋授河南巡撫，擢閩浙總督，皆未行，調授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was transferred to act as governor-general of Huguang, then appointed governor of Henan, promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang — none of which he took up — and finally transferred to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he was transferred to acting governor-general of Huguang, then appointed governor of Henan and promoted to governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang — none of which he actually assumed — before being appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 漢口鎮為商船所聚，苦盜。

translations.literal: Hankou town, where merchant vessels gathered, suffered greatly from bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hankou, where merchant vessels congregated, was plagued by banditry.

sentences.zh: 川匪充鉛船水手，每行劫殺人；

translations.literal: Sichuan bandits served as sailors on lead-transport boats and committed robbery and murder on every voyage;
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan bandits served as sailors on lead-transport boats and committed robbery and murder on every voyage;

sentences.zh: 陝、楚交界奸徒掠販婦女，並為民害：天爵捕治如律，劾失察有司及承審縱延者，悉褫其職。

translations.literal: villains at the Shaanxi-Huguang border abducted and sold women — all were scourges upon the people: Tianjue arrested and punished them according to law, impeached negligent officials and those who delayed trials, and stripped them all of office.
translations.idiomatic: while villains at the Shaanxi-Hubei border abducted and sold women — all scourges upon the people. Tianjue arrested and punished them according to law, impeached negligent officials and those who delayed trials, and stripped them all of office.

sentences.zh: 荊州沿江舊於冬季委員巡緝盜賊，天爵謂屬具文，罷之；

translations.literal: Along the Jingzhou riverbank, winter patrols against bandits had formerly been assigned to commissioners; Tianjue deemed this mere formality and abolished it;
translations.idiomatic: Along the Jingzhou riverbank, winter patrols against bandits had been assigned to commissioners; Tianjue deemed this mere formality and abolished it;

sentences.zh: 遴幹吏暗偵，與地方官掩捕，以獲盜多寡定功過。

translations.literal: he selected capable officials for secret investigation, coordinated with local magistrates for surprise arrests, and determined merit and demerit by the number of bandits captured.
translations.idiomatic: instead selecting capable officials for secret investigation, coordinating surprise arrests with local magistrates, and judging merit by the number of bandits captured.

sentences.zh: 襄陽匪徒傳習牛八邪教，又有天主、十字各教，捕誅數十人。

translations.literal: In Xiangyang, bandits propagated the Niuba heterodox sect, and there were also Catholic and other Christian sects; he arrested and executed several dozen persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiangyang, rebels propagated the Niuba heterodox sect along with Catholic and other Christian sects; he arrested and executed several dozen people.

sentences.zh: 每有疏陳，宣宗輒手詔褒嘉。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted memorials, the Daoguang Emperor would personally issue edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he submitted memorials, the Daoguang Emperor would personally issue edicts of praise.

sentences.zh: 連年水災，濱江、濱漢堤垸多壞，疏請依治黃河法，遇險立挑壩，並以草護堤；

translations.literal: Floods struck year after year, and dikes along the Yangtze and Han rivers were much damaged; he memorialized requesting that, following Yellow River management methods, emergency spur dikes be built at danger points and grass be used to protect the embankments;
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck year after year, damaging dikes along the Yangtze and Han rivers; he memorialized requesting that, following Yellow River management methods, emergency spur dikes be built at danger points and grass be used to protect the embankments;

sentences.zh: 飭治河州縣，有大工解任專治，立限保工，限內失事者罰，紳董亦如之；

translations.literal: he ordered river-administering prefectures and counties that when major works arose, magistrates should be relieved to concentrate on repairs, set time limits with guarantees on the works, penalize failures within the limit, and apply the same to local gentry managers;
translations.idiomatic: he ordered river-administering prefectures and counties that when major works arose, magistrates should be relieved of other duties to concentrate on repairs, set time limits with guarantees on the works, penalize failures within the limit, and apply the same penalties to local gentry managers;

sentences.zh: 漢水多灣曲，立磚石斗門以備蓄洩：並如議行。

translations.literal: the Han River had many bends, so brick and stone sluice gates should be built for storage and release: all were implemented as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: and that brick and stone sluice gates should be built along the Han River's many bends for flood control: all were implemented as proposed.

sentences.zh: 天爵馭吏嚴，多怨者。

translations.literal: Tianjue was strict in governing subordinates, and many bore grudges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue was strict with his subordinates, and many bore grudges against him.

sentences.zh: 二十年，己革大冶知縣孔廣義揭訐多款，天爵置不問。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Kong Guangyi, the dismissed magistrate of Daye, exposed many charges in a public denunciation; Tianjue ignored them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840, Kong Guangyi, the dismissed magistrate of Daye, publicly denounced him on many charges; Tianjue ignored them.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，嚴斥之，議革職留任。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the throne, he was severely rebuked, and dismissal from office with retention of duties was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, he was severely rebuked, and dismissal from office with retention of duties was proposed.

sentences.zh: 尋言官劾天爵酷刑，與廣義言略同，命侍郎麟魁、吳其濬往按，得天爵信任候補知縣楚鏞用非刑，外委黃雲邦誣執良民諸狀，上震怒，褫天爵職，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter censorial officials impeached Tianjue for cruel punishments, largely echoing Guangyi's charges; Ministers Lin Kui and Wu Qijun were sent to investigate and found that Tianjue had trusted the expectant magistrate Chu Yong, who employed illegal torture, and the external appointee Huang Yunbang, who had falsely arrested innocent commoners; the Emperor was greatly angered, stripped Tianjue of office, and banished him to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon censorial officials impeached Tianjue for cruel punishments, largely echoing Guangyi's charges; Ministers Lin Kui and Wu Qijun were sent to investigate and found that Tianjue had trusted the expectant magistrate Chu Yong, who employed illegal torture, and the external appointee Huang Yunbang, who had falsely arrested innocent civilians; the Emperor was enraged, stripped Tianjue of office, and banished him to Yili.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命赴廣東交靖逆將軍奕山差遣，尋免罪，留粵效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was ordered to Guangdong to serve under General Yishan, commander against the rebels, and shortly his sentence was remitted, remaining in Guangdong to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was ordered to Guangdong to serve under General Yishan, commander against the British, and soon his sentence was remitted; he remained in Guangdong to serve.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，予四品頂戴，以知府候補，調江蘇辦理清江防務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was granted a fourth-rank button and served as an expectant prefect, transferred to Jiangsu to manage Qingjiang coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he was granted a fourth-rank button, appointed as an expectant prefect, and transferred to Jiangsu to manage Qingjiang coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 海防事竣，留治淮、揚善後事宜，尋予二品頂戴，​​署漕運總督，兼署南河總督。

translations.literal: When coastal defense affairs were concluded, he remained to handle post-crisis matters in Huai and Yang regions; shortly he was granted a second-rank button, acted as director-general of grain transport, and concurrently acted as director-general of the Southern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When coastal defense affairs were concluded, he remained to handle post-crisis matters in the Huai and Yang regions; he was soon granted a second-rank button, served as acting director-general of grain transport, and concurrently as acting director-general of the Southern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，因濫刑及失察漕書私鐫關防，連被吏議，疏請去職，命以二品頂戴休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because of excessive punishments and failure to detect a grain-transport clerk who had privately carved an official seal, he was repeatedly censured by the Board of Civil Office; he memorialized requesting resignation and was ordered to retire with his second-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843, because of excessive punishments and failure to detect a grain-transport clerk who had privately carved an official seal, he was repeatedly censured; he memorialized requesting resignation and was ordered to retire with his second-rank button.

sentences.zh: 久之，廣西賊起，日益熾。

translations.literal: After a long interval, bandits rose in Guangxi and grew daily more fierce.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, rebels rose in Guangxi and grew fiercer by the day.

sentences.zh: 文宗御極，求知兵大臣，尚書杜受田以天爵對，遂起廣西巡撫，偕欽差大臣李星沅辦賊。

translations.literal: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he sought officials versed in military affairs; Minister Du Shoutian recommended Tianjue, who was therefore recalled as governor of Guangxi to join Imperial Commissioner Li Xingyuan in suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he sought officials versed in military affairs; Minister Du Shoutian recommended Tianjue, who was recalled as governor of Guangxi to join Imperial Commissioner Li Xingyuan in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，親率兵與向榮會剿金田匪洪秀全等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xianfeng, he personally led troops to join Xiang Rong in suppressing the Jintian bandits Hong Xiuquan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1851 he personally led troops to join Xiang Rong in suppressing Hong Xiuquan and the Jintian rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊竄武宣東鄉，合擊於東嶺村，力戰，兵有退者，天爵手刃之，援桴鼓而前，賊始卻。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Dongxiang in Wuxuan; a joint attack was made at Dongling Village in fierce fighting; when some soldiers retreated, Tianjue personally killed them, took up the drumstick to beat the advance, and only then did the rebels withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Dongxiang in Wuxuan; in a joint attack at Dongling Village, when some soldiers began to retreat, Tianjue personally killed them, seized the drumstick to beat the advance, and only then did the rebels fall back.

sentences.zh: 時懷集、賀縣及都康、下雷土司，凌雲、東蘭、橫州、博白並有匪踞，檄各屬力行團練，合力防剿。

translations.literal: At that time bandits also held Huaiji, Hexian, the Dutang and Xialei native offices, Lingyun, Donglan, Hengzhou, and Bobai; he issued orders to all jurisdictions to vigorously organize militia and combine for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels also held Huaiji, Hexian, the Dutang and Xialei native offices, Lingyun, Donglan, Hengzhou, and Bobai; he ordered all jurisdictions to organize militia vigorously and coordinate defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 詔加天爵總督銜，專辦軍務，以布政使勞崇光攝巡撫事。

translations.literal: An edict added the governor-general rank to Tianjue for exclusive charge of military affairs, with Provincial Treasurer Lao Chongguang acting in gubernatorial matters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Tianjue the rank of governor-general for exclusive charge of military affairs, with provincial treasurer Lao Chongguang acting as governor.

sentences.zh: 天爵年近八旬，每戰親臨前敵，惟與李星沅、向榮皆不協。

translations.literal: Tianjue was nearly eighty years old and personally went to the front in every battle, yet he could not cooperate with either Li Xingyuan or Xiang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Though nearly eighty, Tianjue personally went to the front in every battle, yet he could not cooperate with either Li Xingyuan or Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 星沅既疏請特簡總統督師，尋病歿，命天爵暫署欽差大臣。

translations.literal: Xingyuan had already memorialized requesting the special appointment of a supreme commander; he soon died of illness, and Tianjue was ordered temporarily to act as Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan had already memorialized requesting the appointment of a supreme commander; he soon died of illness, and Tianjue was ordered temporarily to act as Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊由武宣竄象州，詔斥天爵等相持日久，不能制賊，褫總督銜，解軍務，回省暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: The rebels fled from Wuxuan to Xiangzhou; an edict rebuked Tianjue and others for prolonged stalemate without subduing the bandits, stripped his governor-general rank, relieved him of military duties, and ordered him back to the province temporarily to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled from Wuxuan to Xiangzhou; an edict rebuked Tianjue and others for prolonged stalemate without defeating the rebels, stripped his governor-general rank, relieved him of military duties, and ordered him back to the provincial capital temporarily to act as governor.

sentences.zh: 洎賽尚阿至軍，議復不合，自陳衰病，詔命來京。

translations.literal: When Sai Shang'a arrived at the army, their counsel again clashed; Tianjue declared his declining health, and an edict ordered him to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Sai Shang'a arrived at the front, their counsel again clashed; Tianjue declared his declining health, and an edict ordered him to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，連召對十一次，極言軍事，文宗為之動容，然方倚賽尚阿，亦未盡用其言。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was summoned for eleven consecutive audiences, speaking exhaustively on military affairs; the Xianfeng Emperor was moved, but as he was then relying on Sai Shang'a, he did not fully adopt Tianjue's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital, he was summoned for eleven consecutive audiences and spoke exhaustively on military affairs; the Xianfeng Emperor was moved, but as he was then relying on Sai Shang'a, he did not fully adopt Tianjue's counsel.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪擾及兩湖，天爵僑居宿州，命偕安徽巡撫蔣文慶治防務。

translations.literal: In the second year, Guangdong bandits disturbed the Two Lakes region; Tianjue was residing in Suzhou and was ordered to join Anhui Governor Jiang Wenqing in managing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, as Guangdong rebels threatened the Two Lakes region, Tianjue was living in Suzhou and was ordered to join Anhui governor Jiang Wenqing in organizing defenses.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏陳廬、鳳為江淮要區，赴正陽關撫舊捻張鳳山等一千二百人用之，請江蘇、山東、安徽、河南舉行團練。

translations.literal: In the third year, he memorialized that Luzhou and Fengyang were vital points on the Jiang-Huai line, went to Zhengyang Pass to recruit twelve hundred former Nian followers led by Zhang Fengshan for service, and requested that Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan organize militia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he memorialized that Luzhou and Fengyang were vital points on the Jiang-Huai line, went to Zhengyang Pass to recruit twelve hundred former Nian followers led by Zhang Fengshan, and requested that Jiangsu, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan organize militia.

sentences.zh: 未幾，安慶陷，文慶死之。

translations.literal: Before long, Anqing fell and Wenqing died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Anqing fell and Jiang Wenqing was killed.

sentences.zh: 命天爵署安徽巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: Tianjue was ordered to act as governor of Anhui, and shortly received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue was appointed acting governor of Anhui and soon received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 江寧亦陷，天爵請扼黃河杜賊北竄，辭巡撫專任兵事。

translations.literal: Jiangning also fell; Tianjue requested to hold the Yellow River to block the bandits' northward flight, resigned the governorship, and devoted himself exclusively to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing also fell, Tianjue requested to hold the Yellow River line against a northern rebel advance, resigned the governorship, and devoted himself exclusively to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 命以兵部侍郎銜督師剿宿州、懷遠、蒙城、靈壁捻匪。

translations.literal: He was ordered, with the rank of vice-minister of war, to command troops in suppressing Nian bandits in Suzhou, Huaiyuan, Mengcheng, and Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered, with the rank of vice-minister of war, to command the suppression of Nian rebels in Suzhou, Huaiyuan, Mengcheng, and Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 北路漸清，進規廬、鳳，擒定遠捻首陸遐齡，散其眾四千餘，被褒賚。

translations.literal: The northern front was gradually pacified; he advanced toward Luzhou and Fengyang, captured the Dingyuan Nian chief Lu Xialing, dispersed his force of more than four thousand, and received commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: As the northern front was gradually pacified, he advanced toward Luzhou and Fengyang, captured the Dingyuan Nian leader Lu Xialing, dispersed his force of more than four thousand men, and received commendation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 疏論廬州知府胡元煒劣跡，請革職逮治，巡撫李嘉端置不問。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the misconduct of Luzhou Prefect Hu Yuanwei, requesting dismissal and arrest; Governor Li Jiaduan ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the misconduct of Luzhou prefect Hu Yuanwei and requested his dismissal and arrest, but Governor Li Jiaduan ignored the matter.

sentences.zh: 元煒通賊內應，廬州陷，江忠源死之。

translations.literal: Yuanwei colluded with the bandits as an inside agent; Luzhou fell and Jiang Zhongyuan died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei had colluded with the rebels as an inside agent; Luzhou fell and Jiang Zhongyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞臨淮關，天爵外遏來賊，內清土匪，孤軍支拄。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits held Linhuai Pass; Tianjue blocked incoming enemies from without and cleared local bandits within, holding the line alone with a solitary army.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels held Linhuai Pass; Tianjue blocked incoming enemies from without and cleared local bandits within, holding the line alone with a solitary force.

sentences.zh: 方奉命往援廬州，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: Just as he was ordered to go to Luzhou's relief, he died of illness in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was ordered to march to Luzhou's relief, he died of illness in camp.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，詔嘉其秉性忠直，勇敢有為，心地品行迥超流俗，追贈尚書銜，依贈官賜卹，特諡文忠，不由內閣擬上；

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; an edict praised his loyal and upright character, his courage and capacity for action, and his moral conduct far above the common run; he was posthumously granted the rank of minister, given funeral benefits according to that rank, and specially given the posthumous name Wenzhong without going through the Grand Secretariat's usual proposal;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply grieved; an edict praised his loyal and upright character, his courage and capacity for action, and his moral conduct far above the common run; he was posthumously granted ministerial rank with funeral benefits accordingly, and was specially given the posthumous name Wenzhong without going through the Grand Secretariat's usual proposal;

sentences.zh: 擢其子光碧都司，賜光岳舉人。

translations.literal: his son Guangbi was promoted to garrison commander, and Guangyue was granted the juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: his son Guangbi was promoted to garrison commander, and Guangyue was granted the juren degree.

sentences.zh: 勞崇光，字辛陔，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Lao Chongguang, styled Xingai, a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Chongguang, styled Xingai, from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Daoguang, he was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1832, entered the Hanlin as a probationary academician, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，出為山西平陽知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he went out to serve as prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was appointed prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 調太原，擢冀寧道，遷廣西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Taiyuan, promoted to the Jining circuit, and moved to surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiyuan, promoted to the Jining circuit intendant, and then appointed judicial commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，奉使赴越南冊封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was dispatched on a mission to Vietnam to confer investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he was dispatched on a mission to Vietnam to confer investiture.

sentences.zh: 事竣入關，值匪亂，駐思恩、南寧，督軍進剿。

translations.literal: When the mission was completed he entered the frontier, encountered bandit turmoil, stationed himself at Si'en and Nanning, and directed troops in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission was completed he re-entered China, encountered bandit unrest, stationed himself at Si'en and Nanning, and directed suppression campaigns.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷湖北布政使，未行而湖南賊李沅發起新寧，仍留廣西治防。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Hubei, but before departing the Hunan bandit Li Yuanfa rose in Xinning, and he remained in Guangxi to manage defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Hubei, but before he could depart the Hunan rebel Li Yuanfa rose in Xinning, and he remained in Guangxi to manage defenses.

sentences.zh: 沅發平，敘功賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Yuanfa was pacified, his merits were recorded and he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanfa was pacified, his merits were recorded and he was awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十年，就授廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he received substantive appointment as provincial treasurer of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he received substantive appointment as provincial treasurer of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 慶遠賊竄武緣、賓州，崇光偕提督向榮會剿。

translations.literal: Bandits from Qingyuan fled to Wuyuan and Binzhou; Chongguang joined Provincial Military Commander Xiang Rong in joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Qingyuan fled to Wuyuan and Binzhou; Chongguang joined military commander Xiang Rong in a joint suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 擒賊首陳勝，又平上林、遷江竄匪，設方略解散匪黨凡數十起。

translations.literal: He captured the bandit chief Chen Sheng, also pacified fleeing bandits in Shanglin and Qianjiang, and by strategic measures dissolved several dozen bandit groups.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the rebel leader Chen Sheng, pacified insurgents who had fled to Shanglin and Qianjiang, and by strategic measures dissolved several dozen rebel groups.

sentences.zh: 撫張家祥收隸部下，改名國樑，後以戰功顯。

translations.literal: He pacified Zhang Jiaxiang and enrolled him under his command, renaming him Guoliang, who later distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Zhang Jiaxiang and enrolled him in his command, renaming him Guoliang; he later distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 尋署巡撫，副將伊克坦布戰歿於桂平，檄總兵周鳳岐赴援。

translations.literal: Shortly he acted as governor; Brigadier-general Yiketanbu was killed in battle at Guiping, and he ordered Major-general Zhou Fengqi to go to his relief.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting governor; brigadier-general Yiketanbu was killed in battle at Guiping, and Chongguang ordered major-general Zhou Fengqi to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 時命李星沅督師，週天爵為巡撫專治軍。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xingyuan was ordered to command the army, and Zhou Tianjue as governor devoted himself exclusively to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xingyuan was ordered to command the campaign, while Zhou Tianjue as governor devoted himself exclusively to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇光仍攝巡撫事，會辦軍務。

translations.literal: Chongguang still acted in gubernatorial matters and jointly handled military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang continued to handle gubernatorial affairs and jointly managed military operations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，大學士賽尚阿代星沅，而鄒鳴鶴繼為巡撫，崇光會辦如故，平西林、博白、懷集竄賊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a replaced Xingyuan, and Zou Minghe succeeded as governor; Chongguang continued joint handling as before and pacified fleeing bandits in Xilin, Bobai, and Huaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a replaced Xingyuan, and Zou Minghe succeeded as governor; Chongguang continued his joint duties and pacified insurgents who had fled to Xilin, Bobai, and Huaiji.

sentences.zh: 廣東賊顏品瑤擾南寧、太平，崇光駐兵南邕，與廣東軍合擊，屢戰皆捷，品瑤就殲，又平貴縣賊，被優敘。

translations.literal: The Guangdong bandit Yan Pinyao harassed Nanning and Taiping; Chongguang stationed troops at Nanyong and joined Guangdong forces in attack, winning repeated victories; Pinyao was destroyed, and bandits in Guixian were also pacified; he received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong rebel Yan Pinyao harassed Nanning and Taiping; Chongguang stationed troops at Nanyong and joined Guangdong forces in attack, winning repeated victories; Pinyao was destroyed and rebels in Guixian were also pacified; he received preferential commendation.

sentences.zh: 偕左江鎮總兵谷韞燦平白山賊，舉行南、太、泗、鎮四府團練，殲顏品瑤餘黨於靈山，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Together with Zuojiang garrison commander Gu Yuncan he pacified bandits on Baishan, organized militia in the four prefectures of Nanning, Taiping, Si, and Zhen, destroyed Pinyao's remnant followers at Lingshan, and was granted the first-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zuojiang garrison commander Gu Yuncan he pacified rebels on Baishan, organized militia in the four prefectures of Nanning, Taiping, Si, and Zhen, destroyed Pinyao's remnant followers at Lingshan, and was granted the first-rank button.

sentences.zh: 二年，駐梧州，會廣東軍剿艇匪。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was stationed at Wuzhou and joined Guangdong forces in suppressing boat bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was stationed at Wuzhou and joined Guangdong forces in suppressing boat pirates.

sentences.zh: 尋金田賊洪秀全等永安突圍出犯桂林，命崇光回援，至則賊已北竄，連陷興安、全州，偕總兵和春追擊之，賊遂入湖南。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the Jintian bandits Hong Xiuquan and others broke out of Yong'an and attacked Guilin; Chongguang was ordered back to relieve it, but upon arrival the bandits had already fled north, successively taking Xing'an and Quanzhou; he joined Major-general He Chun in pursuit, and the bandits then entered Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jintian rebels Hong Xiuquan and others broke out of Yong'an and attacked Guilin; Chongguang was ordered back to relieve the city, but upon arrival the rebels had already fled north, successively taking Xing'an and Quanzhou; he joined major-general He Chun in pursuit, and the rebels then entered Hunan.

sentences.zh: 會雲貴總督吳文鎔疏稱崇光有膽略血性，請重其事權，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Governor-General Wu Wenrong of Yunnan and Guizhou memorialized that Chongguang possessed courage, boldness, and fighting spirit, requesting that his authority be strengthened, and he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Wu Wenrong memorialized that Chongguang possessed courage, boldness, and fighting spirit, requesting that his authority be strengthened, and he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 上疏略曰：「桂林雖解圍，賊氛不遠，群情尚復驚疑，增兵置防，皆非倉卒能辦。

translations.literal: He memorialized in summary: "Although Guilin has been relieved, the bandit threat is not far off, and public sentiment remains alarmed and uncertain; increasing troops and setting defenses cannot be accomplished hastily.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in summary: "Although Guilin has been relieved, the rebel threat is not far off, and public sentiment remains alarmed and uncertain; increasing troops and setting defenses cannot be accomplished hastily.

sentences.zh: 惟就現有兵力佈置，省標調赴各處者，次第撤回，駐防城內，遴選練丁分扼城外要隘。

translations.literal: We can only deploy existing forces: provincial banner troops dispatched elsewhere should be gradually recalled to garrison the city, and selected militia should be posted at key passes outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: We can only deploy existing forces: provincial banner troops dispatched elsewhere should be gradually recalled to garrison the city, and selected militia should be posted at key passes outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 激勵團練以作民氣，招撫流亡以復民力，訓練兵勇以肅軍紀，搜緝土匪以靖內奸。

translations.literal: Encourage militia to raise popular morale, recruit and pacify refugees to restore popular strength, train soldiers to enforce military discipline, and hunt down local bandits to quell internal traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Encourage militia to raise popular morale, recruit and pacify refugees to restore popular strength, train soldiers to enforce military discipline, and hunt down local bandits to quell internal enemies.

sentences.zh: 各屬遊匪、土匪不時蠢動，額兵不敷分撥，鼓舞團練，以資捍衛而備援剿。」

translations.literal: Roaming bandits and local bandits in various jurisdictions stir from time to time, and regular troops are insufficient for distribution; invigorate militia to provide defense and prepare for relief and suppression."
translations.idiomatic: Roaming and local bandits in various jurisdictions stir from time to time, and regular troops are insufficient for distribution; invigorate militia to provide defense and prepare for relief and suppression operations."

sentences.zh: 時賽尚阿既黜，崇光專任廣西軍務，詔以匪雖已出粵境舊巢穴，慮渠魁踞之為回竄地步，責以搜捕黨羽。

translations.literal: By then Sai Shang'a had been dismissed; Chongguang had sole charge of Guangxi military affairs. An edict stated that although the bandits had left their old lair in Guangdong territory, there was concern that rebel chiefs might occupy it as a base for return raids, and he was charged with hunting down their followers.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sai Shang'a had been dismissed and Chongguang had sole charge of Guangxi military affairs. An edict noted that although the rebels had left their old lair in Guangdong territory, there was concern that rebel chiefs might occupy it as a base for return raids, and he was charged with hunting down their followers.

sentences.zh: 三年，洪秀全等既踞江寧，分黨北犯中原。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hong Xiuquan and others having seized Jiangning, they sent factions north to invade the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, after Hong Xiuquan and others seized Nanjing, they sent factions north to invade the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 兵事日棘，朝廷不暇顧及邊遠，廣西伏莽時起，旋滅旋萌，餉絀兵單，惟恃團練，不能大創賊。

translations.literal: Military affairs grew daily more pressing; the court had no leisure to attend to remote borders. Latent bandits in Guangxi rose from time to time, extinguished only to sprout again; funds were short and troops few, relying solely on militia, unable to inflict a major blow on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs grew daily more pressing; the court had no leisure to attend to remote borders. Latent insurgents in Guangxi rose from time to time, extinguished only to sprout again; funds were short and troops few, relying solely on militia, unable to inflict a major defeat on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 崇光且剿且撫，支拄數載。

translations.literal: Chongguang alternately suppressed and pacified, holding the situation for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang alternately suppressed and pacified, holding the situation together for several years.

sentences.zh: 洎英人踞廣州後，廣東賊氛复熾。

translations.literal: When the English occupied Guangzhou, bandit activity in Guangdong flared up again.
translations.idiomatic: After the British occupied Guangzhou, rebel activity in Guangdong flared up again.

sentences.zh: 艇匪竄擾廣西，潯州、柳州、慶遠、梧州、南寧相繼陷。

translations.literal: Boat bandits raided Guangxi; Xunzhou, Liuzhou, Qingyuan, Wuzhou, and Nanning fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Boat pirates raided Guangxi; Xunzhou, Liuzhou, Qingyuan, Wuzhou, and Nanning fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 近地土匪益起，屢逼桂林。

translations.literal: Local bandits in the vicinity rose increasingly and repeatedly threatened Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits in the vicinity rose increasingly and repeatedly threatened Guilin.

sentences.zh: 軍中多降將，心皆叵測。

translations.literal: The army had many surrendered generals, all with inscrutable intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The army had many surrendered generals, all with unreliable loyalties.

sentences.zh: 崇光乞師於湖南，七年，駱秉章令蔣益澧率湘軍赴援，屢破賊，復興安、靈川，入屯省城，乃誅反側，易守軍，桂林始安。

translations.literal: Chongguang requested troops from Hunan; in the seventh year, Luo Bingzhang ordered Jiang Yili to lead Hunan Army forces to his relief; they repeatedly defeated the bandits, recovered Xing'an and Lingchuan, entered and garrisoned the provincial capital, then executed disloyal elements and replaced the garrison troops, and Guilin was finally secured.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang requested troops from Hunan; in 1857 Luo Bingzhang ordered Jiang Yili to lead Hunan Army forces to his relief; they repeatedly defeated the rebels, recovered Xing'an and Lingchuan, entered and garrisoned the provincial capital, executed disloyal elements and replaced the garrison troops, and Guilin was finally secured.

sentences.zh: 八年，奏留益澧在廣西勦賊，連擊艇匪於平樂令公渡、五塘，大破之，斬馘萬餘，由是艇匪始衰，慶遠、柳州相繼复。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he memorialized to retain Yili in Guangxi to suppress bandits; they repeatedly attacked boat bandits at Linggong Ford and Wutang in Pingle, inflicting a great defeat and killing more than ten thousand; thereafter boat bandits began to decline, and Qingyuan and Liuzhou were recovered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he memorialized to retain Jiang Yili in Guangxi to suppress rebels; they repeatedly attacked boat pirates at Linggong Ford and Wutang in Pingle, inflicting a great defeat and killing more than ten thousand; thereafter boat piracy began to decline, and Qingyuan and Liuzhou were recovered in succession.

sentences.zh: 九年，調廣東巡撫，兼署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to governor of Guangdong and concurrently acted as governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he was transferred to governor of Guangdong and concurrently served as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 英軍猶踞省城，前任總督黃宗漢、巡撫耆齡等，皆駐外縣不敢入。

translations.literal: British forces still held the provincial capital; the former governor-general Huang Zonghan, governor Qiling, and others all stayed in outer counties and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: British forces still held the provincial capital; former governor-general Huang Zonghan, governor Qiling, and others all stayed in outer counties and dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 崇光至，坦然入城，與敵軍狎居。

translations.literal: When Chongguang arrived, he calmly entered the city and lived on familiar terms with the enemy forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongguang arrived, he calmly entered the city and lived on familiar terms with the enemy forces.

sentences.zh: 尋實授總督，迭遣將禦湖南、江西竄匪，擊走之。

translations.literal: Shortly he received substantive appointment as governor-general, repeatedly dispatched generals to repel bandits fleeing from Hunan and Jiangxi, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received substantive appointment as governor-general, repeatedly dispatched generals to repel rebels fleeing from Hunan and Jiangxi, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 本境土寇時起，皆不久撲滅。

translations.literal: Local bandits within the province rose from time to time but were all soon suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits within the province rose from time to time but were all soon suppressed.

sentences.zh: 與廣西軍會剿艇匪，梧州、潯州賊匪漸清。

translations.literal: Joining Guangxi forces in suppressing boat bandits, bandit activity in Wuzhou and Xunzhou was gradually cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Guangxi forces in suppressing boat pirates, rebel activity in Wuzhou and Xunzhou was gradually cleared.

sentences.zh: 至十一年，英法聯軍犯京師，和議成，廣州敵軍始退。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year, the Anglo-French allied forces attacked the capital; when peace was concluded, the enemy forces in Guangzhou finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: By 1861 the Anglo-French allied forces had attacked the capital; when peace was concluded, the enemy forces in Guangzhou finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以失察都司陶昌培、知縣許慶鎔營私納賄，降三級調用，命仍以一品頂戴赴貴州按事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, for failure to detect Battalion Commander Tao Changpei and Magistrate Xu Qingrong in private corruption and bribe-taking, he was demoted three ranks and transferred, but ordered still to proceed to Guizhou with his first-rank button to investigate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, for failure to detect battalion commander Tao Changpei and magistrate Xu Qingrong in private corruption and bribe-taking, he was demoted three ranks and transferred, but ordered still to proceed to Guizhou with his first-rank button to investigate affairs.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫耆齡、御史華祝三復劾崇光任用非人，調度乖方，詔命自陳，下署總督晏端書、提督昆壽察按，得免議。

translations.literal: The former governor Qiling and Censor Hua Zhu again impeached Chongguang for employing unfit persons and erratic command; an edict ordered him to explain himself; Acting Governor-General Yan Duanshu and Military Commander Kunshou were sent to investigate, and he was cleared of charges.
translations.idiomatic: Former governor Qiling and censor Hua Zhu again impeached Chongguang for employing unfit persons and erratic command; an edict ordered him to explain himself; acting governor-general Yan Duanshu and military commander Kunshou were sent to investigate, and he was cleared of charges.

sentences.zh: 尋授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南自總督潘鐸被戕，巡撫徐之銘結回酋以自保，張凱嵩繼署總督，久不至，以規避黜，命崇光代之。

translations.literal: Since Governor-General Pan Duo was assassinated in Yunnan, Governor Xu Zhiming had allied with Hui chieftains for self-protection; Zhang Kaisong succeeded as acting governor-general but long failed to arrive and was dismissed for evasion; Chongguang was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Governor-General Pan Duo was assassinated in Yunnan, Governor Xu Zhiming had allied with Muslim chieftains for self-protection; Zhang Kaisong succeeded as acting governor-general but long failed to arrive and was dismissed for evasion; Chongguang was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 崇光至貴州，會粵匪石達開餘黨陷綏陽，督兵擊走之，遂駐貴陽。

translations.literal: Chongguang reached Guizhou, where Guangdong bandit remnants of Shi Dakai's faction had seized Suiyang; he directed troops to drive them off and then stationed himself at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang reached Guizhou, where remnants of Shi Dakai's Guangdong rebels had seized Suiyang; he directed troops to drive them off and then established headquarters at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 三年春，土匪、苗匪屢來犯，偕巡撫張亮基勒兵固守，賊敗退。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, local bandits and Miao bandits repeatedly attacked; together with Governor Zhang Liangji he pressed the troops to hold firm, and the bandits were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1864 local bandits and Miao rebels repeatedly attacked; together with governor Zhang Liangji he pressed the troops to hold firm, and the rebels were defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時雲南叛回猶雜處省城，議者皆言不可遽往。

translations.literal: At that time rebellious Hui still mingled within the Yunnan provincial capital; advisers all said he should not go there hastily.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebellious Muslims still mingled within the Yunnan provincial capital; advisers all said he should not go there hastily.

sentences.zh: 崇光迳行，軍民父老喜，迎於郊，回眾始稍斂。

translations.literal: Chongguang went directly; soldiers, civilians, and elders rejoiced and welcomed him in the suburbs; the Hui masses then began to restrain themselves somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang went directly; soldiers, civilians, and elders rejoiced and welcomed him in the suburbs; the Muslim communities then began to restrain themselves somewhat.

sentences.zh: 逆首馬榮、馬連升踞曲靖為巢穴。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs Ma Rong and Ma Liansheng held Qujing as their base.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders Ma Rong and Ma Liansheng held Qujing as their base.

sentences.zh: 崇光知候補道岑毓英、降回總兵馬如龍可用，四年春，令參將馮世興與二人合師攻克曲靖，擒榮、連升等斬以徇，遂收馬龍、尋甸，迤東肅清，遣提督趙德光克平江外賊巢，复廣順，進克貴州，黔西大定。

translations.literal: Chongguang knew that the expectant circuit intendant Cen Yuying and the surrendered Hui Major-general Ma Rulong were usable; in the spring of the fourth year he ordered Brigade Commander Feng Shixing to join the two in a combined force that captured Qujing, seized Rong, Liansheng, and others and executed them as a warning, then recovered Malong and Xundian, pacified eastern Yunnan, dispatched Military Commander Zhao Deguang to level bandit nests beyond the rivers, recovered Guangshun, advanced to take Guizhou, and secured western Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang knew that expectant circuit intendant Cen Yuying and the surrendered Muslim major-general Ma Rulong were capable commanders; in the spring of 1865 he ordered brigade commander Feng Shixing to join them in a combined force that captured Qujing, seized Rong, Liansheng, and others and executed them as a warning, then recovered Malong and Xundian and pacified eastern Yunnan; he dispatched military commander Zhao Deguang to destroy rebel nests beyond the rivers, recovered Guangshun, advanced into Guizhou, and secured western Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，复普洱及思茅，雲南軍事漸利。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Pu'er and Simao were recovered, and Yunnan military affairs gradually improved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Pu'er and Simao were recovered, and the military situation in Yunnan gradually improved.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，優詔賜卹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died, and a special edict granted posthumous benefits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he died, and a special edict granted posthumous benefits.

sentences.zh: 嘉其「沈毅有為，歷官兩廣、雲貴，皆不避艱險，俾地方日有起色」，贈太子太保，諡文毅。

translations.literal: He was praised for being "steadfast and capable, holding office in the Two Guangs and Yunnan-Guizhou without shunning hardship, enabling local conditions to improve day by day"; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for being "steadfast and capable, holding office in the Two Guangs and Yunnan-Guizhou without shunning hardship, enabling local conditions to improve steadily"; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 廣西請建專祠，雲、貴祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Guangxi requested a special temple in his honor; Yunnan and Guizhou enshrined him in the temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi requested a special temple in his honor; Yunnan and Guizhou enshrined him in the temple of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 論曰：粵匪之起也，始由疆臣玩誤，繼復將帥不和。

translations.literal: The commentary states: The rise of the Guangdong bandits began with frontier officials' negligence and complacency, and was followed by discord among generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: The rise of the Guangdong rebels began with frontier officials' negligence and complacency, followed by discord among generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 李星沅、週天爵皆素以忠勤著，文宗採時譽而付以重任，於軍事皆不得要領。

translations.literal: Li Xingyuan and Zhou Tianjue were both known for loyalty and diligence; the Xianfeng Emperor, taking their contemporary reputations, entrusted them with heavy responsibilities, yet in military affairs neither grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan and Zhou Tianjue were both known for loyalty and diligence; the Xianfeng Emperor, swayed by their contemporary reputations, entrusted them with heavy responsibilities, yet in military affairs neither grasped the essentials.

sentences.zh: 及易以賽尚阿，而敗壞益甚，虎兕出柙，遂不可製矣。

translations.literal: When they were replaced by Sai Shang'a, the deterioration grew worse; tigers and rhinoceroses escaped their cages, and could no longer be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When they were replaced by Sai Shang'a, the deterioration grew worse; once the tigers and rhinoceroses escaped their cages, they could no longer be controlled.

sentences.zh: 勞崇光久在兵間，洪秀全北竄後已不顧舊巢，然伏莽四起，終賴湘軍之力，數年而後克定；

translations.literal: Lao Chongguang had long been in military affairs; after Hong Xiuquan fled north he no longer cared for his old lair, yet latent bandits rose on all sides, and in the end it depended on the Hunan Army's strength — only after several years was order finally restored;
translations.idiomatic: Lao Chongguang had long been in military affairs; after Hong Xiuquan fled north the old rebel base was abandoned, yet latent insurgents rose on all sides, and in the end order depended on the Hunan Army — only after several years was the province finally pacified;

sentences.zh: 其於廣東、雲南皆受事於萬難措置之時，履虎不咥，權略有足稱焉。

translations.literal: in Guangdong and Yunnan he took office at times when nothing could be easily arranged; he walked among tigers without being bitten, and his resourcefulness is worthy of note.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong and Yunnan he took office at times when nothing could be easily arranged; he walked among tigers without being bitten, and his resourcefulness is worthy of note.
